label: Homology: Holes As Linear Algebra
notes: Open by framing the chapter as a translation problem. The visible objects are simplices and holes, but the computation runs through vector spaces, boundary matrices, kernels, images, and quotient groups. The verified source span is printed pages 79 through 102, with exercises used only for orientation.

label: From Simplices To Chain Groups
notes: Make the algebra concrete by naming the basis elements. A p-chain is a finite formal sum of p-simplices, and over F2 the coefficients act like on and off switches. The important move is that geometry has become a coordinate vector.

label: Addition Cancels Shared Pieces
notes: Use the paired triangles to show why F2 addition is natural for computation. When two chains share an edge, that edge appears twice and disappears. This is the same cancellation that makes symmetric difference and mod two arithmetic agree.

label: Boundary Maps
notes: Present the boundary operator as the machine that drops dimension. Vertices are the boundary of an edge, edges are the boundary of a triangle, and the linear extension is what lets one assemble complicated chains from simple columns.

label: Why Partial Partial Equals Zero
notes: Slow down on this lemma because it licenses the quotient definition later. Each lower-dimensional face of a simplex appears exactly twice in the boundary of the boundary. Over F2 those paired appearances cancel, so every boundary is automatically a cycle.

label: Cycles, Boundaries, Homology
notes: Distinguish the two subgroups before taking the quotient. Cycles are chains whose boundary has vanished, while boundaries are cycles already explained by a higher-dimensional chain. Homology keeps the cycles left over after those explained ones are identified.

label: Betti Numbers Read The Shape
notes: Read the Betti vector as a compact summary rather than a full classification. The table shows that components, tunnels, voids, and filled regions contribute in different dimensions. The rank formula is the computational bridge from matrices to shape.

label: Chain Maps Preserve Boundaries
notes: Explain functoriality as a compatibility rule. A map of complexes induces linear maps on chains, and the square says mapping then taking boundary agrees with taking boundary then mapping. Without this commutation, homology classes would not be transported reliably.

label: Boundary Matrices
notes: Turn the boundary operator into a board of zeros and ones. Rows name lower-dimensional simplices, columns name higher-dimensional simplices, and a one records incidence. The product check D1 times D2 equals zero is the matrix version of boundary squared zero.

label: Reduction Worked Example
notes: Walk through the small circle example as a rank computation. Column operations over F2 preserve rank, and the reduced D1 matrix has two pivots. With three edges and three vertices, the formula gives one connected component and one independent loop.

label: Euler-Poincare Tracker
notes: Use Euler-Poincare as an audit trail. Alternating simplex counts and alternating Betti counts agree because ranks cancel across the chain complex. It is not a complete invariant, but it is an excellent consistency check for a homology computation.

label: Relative Homology Of A Pair
notes: Describe relative chains as chains of K with the subcomplex K0 treated as invisible. Boundaries are allowed to land in K0, so a chain that was not an absolute cycle can become a relative cycle. This is the algebra of collapsing the reference part of the space.

label: Excision As Local Replacement
notes: Present excision as permission to replace local clutter without changing the relative answer. Once the same complement is kept, the lower-right incidence block carries the relative computation. The slide's check names that the relative quotient ranks match.

label: Exactness: Image Equals Kernel
notes: Exactness should sound operational: everything that dies at the next map was born from the previous map. The toy sequence verifies image equals kernel at the middle term. This is stronger than merely saying the composite is zero.

label: Long Exact Sequence And Connecting Map
notes: Focus on the connecting map as the non-obvious arrow. A relative cycle may have a boundary inside K0, and that boundary becomes a lower-dimensional class in K0. The long exact sequence organizes the absolute and relative groups into one diagnostic line.

label: Snake / Mayer-Vietoris Recap
notes: Close by linking the chapter's two global devices. The snake construction turns short exact sequences of chain complexes into long exact sequences in homology, and Mayer-Vietoris applies this to a union. The final message is divide, compute, and glue through exactness.
